Life-Altering Experiences: You Take The Risk
I believe taking LSD to be a very maturing experience ... Sometimes, way too maturing. I want to share what happened to me sometime during my teen-hood, on a wild-weekend with friends. Not a Bad trip, but a very reasonable discovery of one self.
In a Novemberish weekend, I was hanging with some of my closest friends and having a great time. At the time I was 20 and beginning to enjoy my independence as I left home to go to university. I was expecting more of my friends that weekend, one of them in particular a close childhood buddy, we treated each other as brothers (not in a family-like, always quarreling way, lovingly and supportingly). He arrived, happyness to everyone, all is good.
We took some LSD and other substances that time, but before that I was feeling I needed love in my life, maybe the physical type, I wanted to be with someone and share my ever-growing and maturing self. But somehow it wasn't happening. Every girl I met just 'had' a little something that made my desire go away, as I 'tested' every love-willing girl for their personality and such. Couldn't help it, I do that. And then, on a pleasurable moment of friendship, I had a sort of an awakening feeling, like a little-stronger heart pump that said : 'You Like' (can't say Love there instead of Like, still can't). But that feeling was directed towards that childhood, brother/best-friend of mine. Yes, I discovered homosexuality in me, was never prepared for that, and for a while then, didn't want to perceive it ... Anyhow ... This relates to LSD. Taking it somehow unleashed a logical process that I (I think) wasn't aware of. But anyways, I was never really mature, neither sexually neither on any other manner, was always child-like in many ways, and that 'growth' proved to be healthy, in itself an extremely valuable asset, but that I couldn't cope very well with, somehow, in these days (I'm 24 now) I still can't deal with it very naturally, but I've been taking some willing responsible steps towards a re-opening of my being, and I hope it all goes for the best.
The 4 years that I took to begin to mature and accept the GAY idea were in many ways, a bad trip. Today, the 'bad' part is being replaced and a leveled, self-loving and comprehensible person is appearing.
I respect LSD.
